Subject: Question on rerank/classifier billing model

Hi Marcus —

Thanks for the demo yesterday. As we scope the pilot, procurement asked a couple of specific questions about how rerank and classifier calls are billed:

- Do you meter rerank scoring per candidate evaluated (e.g., 1 request scoring 100 items = 100 scoring units) or per API call?
- For classifiers that return per-item labels, is the billing based on tokens or per-labelled item?
- How does batching impact unit pricing and discounts for committed monthly usage?

We’re trying to build a TCO model; any clear examples or a simple rate card snippet would help. Attaching our current traffic estimate: ~500k classifier decisions/month, ~200k rerank candidates (average 12 candidates/request).

Appreciate a quick note so procurement can start the SRM review.

Best,
Claire

Subject: Re: Question on rerank/classifier billing model

Hi Claire —

Great questions — happy to clarify. Short answers up front:

- Rerank: billed per scored candidate (so 1 call scoring 12 candidates = 12 scoring units).
- Classifier: billed per decision/label emitted. Token costs for the underlying model are accounted for separately on token-based generation endpoints; for our classifier endpoints we expose a per-label price that normalizes typical token usage.
- Batching: batching reduces per-item unit cost because the system amortizes model overhead and KV cache hits; we provide a small effective credit when requests are batched (e.g., 10% effective savings at typical batch sizes) and larger committed discounts for reserved capacity.

I’m attaching a trimmed rate card for reference and looping in Dev to provide a short technical note on how we count candidates and what happens with early-exit rerank optimizations. Stephanie will call out discounting options for committed spend.

Next steps: I can put together a simple cost table for your numbers this week. Does Thursday 11am PT work for a 30-min sync?

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Question on rerank/classifier billing model

Claire — quick technical clarification from the runtime team:

- Metering detail: our rerank endpoint increments a counter per candidate scored. If you send a request with candidates array of length N, we count N scoring units regardless of whether you request top-k or a full sort.
- Short-circuiting: if you use early-exit (stop after top-1) in the client and our SDK avoids scoring remaining candidates, those skipped candidates won’t be counted. Early-exit requires the "score_stream" feature flag in the SDK so the runtime can accept partial scoring semantics.
- Classifier endpoints: each item that returns a label or probability vector is 1 billing unit. If the classifier additionally emits an explanation text field (longer tokens), token charges for that text are billed on top of the per-decision charge only if you opt into the verbose-explain mode.
- Batching behavior: server-side batching groups items across concurrent requests; the billing unit is still per-item but batching reduces per-item latency and can reduce the effective cost if you use our dedicated reserved pools because commit discounts are applied to the monthly invoice.

If you want, I can produce a worked example for your stated volumes (500k decisions, 200k rerank candidates at avg 12 candidates/request).

—Dev

Hi Claire —

Attaching a concise rate card and a sample statement-of-amounts (SOA_pricing_breakout.xlsx). Highlights:

- Hosted public pricing (baseline): rerank scoring $0.0012 per candidate, classifier decision $0.0020 per item (these are illustrative for the template; final pricing will be on the quote).
- Committed 12-month reserved option: tiered discounts up to 35% depending on ARR commitment. For your volumes we typically qualify for the 15–20% band.
- Breakpoints: price steps at 500k, 1M, 5M monthly decisions (each step reduces per-item price by ~8–12% depending on overall commit).
- Bundles: we can include token credits for explanation text or rerank metadata as part of the reserved package if you want a blended effective rate.

I’ve attached the PDF rate card and a simple workbook with the two scenarios. Marcus — I set a placeholder for a Thursday 11am PT call; if that time works, I’ll join and bring a short pricing slide.
